rules.cwe_name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')
rules.description: Attacker-controlled object keys modify Object prototype attributes.
Iterating over an object with a user-controlled .length property can cause indefinite looping.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
rules.description: Recursively merging a user-controlled object into another object can allow an attacker to modify the built-in Object prototype, and possibly escalate to remote code execution or cross-site scripting.
If an object literal has two properties with the same name, the second property overwrites the first one, which makes the code hard to understand and error-prone.

rules.cwe_name: Inclusion of Web Functionality from an Untrusted Source
rules.description: Including functionality from an untrusted source may allow an attacker to control the functionality and execute arbitrary code.
Allowing writes to arbitrary properties of an object may lead to denial-of-service attacks.
DOM functions that act like 'eval' and execute strings as code are dangerous and impede program analysis and understanding. Consequently, they should not be used.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions
rules.description: Calling a method with a user-controlled name may dispatch to an unexpected target, which could cause an exception.
Assigning to a property of a primitive value has no effect and may trigger a runtime error.

rules.cwe_name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
rules.description: If the 'X-Frame-Options' setting is not provided, a malicious user may be able to overlay their own UI on top of the site by using an iframe.
